BACKPORT: mac80211: Add TXQ scheduling API This adds an API to mac80211 to handle scheduling of TXQs. The interface between driver and mac80211 for TXQ handling is changed by adding two new functions: ieee80211_next_txq(), which will return the next TXQ to schedule in the current round-robin rotation, and ieee80211_return_txq(), which the driver uses to indicate that it has finished scheduling a TXQ (which will then be put back in the scheduling rotation if it isn't empty). The driver must call ieee80211_txq_schedule_start() at the start of each scheduling session, and ieee80211_txq_schedule_end() at the end. The API then guarantees that the same TXQ is not returned twice in the same session (so a driver can loop on ieee80211_next_txq() without worrying about breaking the loop. Usage of the new API is optional, so drivers can be ported one at a time. In this patch, the actual scheduling performed by mac80211 is simple round-robin, but a subsequent commit adds airtime fairness awareness to the scheduler. BACKPORT: mac80211: Add airtime accounting and scheduling to TXQs This adds airtime accounting and scheduling to the mac80211 TXQ scheduler. A new callback, ieee80211_sta_register_airtime(), is added that drivers can call to report airtime usage for stations. When airtime information is present, mac80211 will schedule TXQs (through ieee80211_next_txq()) in a way that enforces airtime fairness between active stations. This scheduling works the same way as the ath9k in-driver airtime fairness scheduling. If no airtime usage is reported by the driver, the scheduler will default to round-robin scheduling. For drivers that don't control TXQ scheduling in software, a new API function, ieee80211_txq_may_transmit(), is added which the driver can use to check if the TXQ is eligible for transmission, or should be throttled to enforce fairness. Calls to this function must also be enclosed in ieee80211_txq_schedule_{start,end}() calls to ensure proper locking. The API ieee80211_txq_may_transmit() also ensures that TXQ list will be aligned aginst driver's own round-robin scheduler list. i.e it rotates the TXQ list till it makes the requested node becomes the first entry in TXQ list. Thus both the TXQ list and driver's list are in sync. BACKPORT: ath10k: migrate to mac80211 txq scheduling ath10k maintains common txqs list for all stations. This txq management can be removed by migrating to mac80211 txq APIs and let mac80211 handle txqs reordering based on reported airtime. By doing this, txq fairness maintained in ath10k i.e processing N frames per txq is removed. By adapting to mac80211 APIs, ath10k will support mac80211 based airtime fairness algorithm. UPSTREAM: mac80211: make ieee80211_schedule_txq schedule empty TXQs Currently there is no way for the driver to signal to mac80211 that it should schedule a TXQ even if there are no packets on the mac80211 part of that queue. This is problematic if the driver has an internal retry queue to deal with software A-MPDU retry. This patch changes the behavior of ieee80211_schedule_txq to always schedule the queue, as its only user (ath9k) seems to expect such behavior already: it calls this function on tx status and on powersave wakeup whenever its internal retry queue is not empty. Also add an extra argument to ieee80211_return_txq to get the same behavior. This fixes an issue on ath9k where tx queues with packets to retry (and no new packets in mac80211) would not get serviced. CHROMIUM: mac80211: Add airtime based firmware queue size limit Limit the number of frames that can be released to firmware. In order for the Fq_CoDel integrated in mac80211 layer operates effectively to control excessive latency, the CoDel algorithm requires an accurate measure of how long the packets stays in the queue, aka sojourn time, and expect lower layer (firmware) to have a thin queue. However, most 802.11ac chipsets offload tasks such TX aggregation to firmware or hardware, thus have a deep lower layer queue. Due to this deep lower layer queue, packets only stay in mac80211 layer transiently before released to firmware, so the sojourn time measured by CoDel in mac80211 layer is always lower than the latency target, even when the firmware queue causes excessive latency. This patch implements an airtime based firmware queue limit to make CoDel works effectively with wireless driver that utilized firmware/hardware offloading. It only allows each txq to release just enough packets to form 1-2 large aggregations, and keep the rest of frames in mac80211 layer to be controlled by CoDel. BUG=b:131197056 TEST=wireless stress and latency under load test. CHROMIUM: adapter: Prevent cleaning up temporary devices during active scanning. bluetoothd is supposed to clean up temporary devices after 3 minutes of scanning absence, the logic was implemented using a timer that would be triggered 3 minutes after the last scanning stops. This could cause the following problem: 1. Chrome starts scanning. 2. Chrome stops scanning (timer starts counting to 3 minutes). 3. Nothing happens for 2 minutes 50 seconds. 4. Chrome starts scanning. 5. 10 seconds later, the timer created by step 2 triggers bluetoothd to clean up the scanning result (in the middle of Chrome scanning session). 6. Chrome stops scanning. In this change we cancel the timer if it exists when a new scanning starts. BUG=chromium:959306 TEST=manual tests via bluetoothctl with the following steps: 1. Turn scanning on 2. Turn scanning off after some devices have been discovered. 3. Count to 2 minutes 50 seconds. 4. Turn scanning on again. 5. Observe that the devices are not removed crossing the 3 minute mark. 6. Turn scanning off. 7. Wait for 3 minutes. 8. Observe the temp devices are deleted in the terminal. 9. The 'devices' command should return empty list. Increase timeout when fingers leave Sometimes when scrolling or swiping with multiple fingers, one finger will leave the edge of the touchpad before the others, causing the gesture with fewer fingers to be detected. This CL increases the timeout after an actively gesturing finger leaves before another gesture can be detected. It also now only suspends gesture detection when it is an actively gesturing finger that leaves. If a non-gesturing thumb or palm leaves the touchpad, gesture detection is not delayed. Remove close distance check for swipes With bigger touchpads on newer devices, people tend to spread their fingers out further when performing three or four finger swipes. As a result, the distance check to make sure all the fingers are close together has caused some missed gestures - three finger swipes that look like 2 finger scrolls or four finger swipes that look like three finger swipes. The distance check adds little value in filtering out palms for swipes, because swipes already require the fingers to be moving a significant distance in the same direction. This CL removes the distance check for three and four finger swipes entirely. hci: Choose legacy advertising over extended advertising commands. Bluetooth 5.0 (Vol 2, Part E, section 3.1.1) disallows mixing of legacy and extended advertising commands. However, there is no command to explicitly choose which mode (legacy or extended) the host wants to use, but rather the first advertising command will determine whether legacy or extended advertising commands will be allowed for the rest of the controller's lifetime (until Reset). So we call an arbitrary read-only legacy advertising command very early to tell the controller that we want to use the legacy advertising commands instead of extended advertising commands. Without specifying legacy vs extended commands very early, we might hit an unexpected Command Disallowed later on. For example, LE Set Scan Parameters hits Command Disallowed error on Thunder Peak. CRAS: dev_io - Add the overrun op threshold On grunt, the number of frames an input node reads once is decided by a period size, whose default vaule is 1024. According to the latest overrun ops, if the device's hw_level is larger than 2 * largest_cb_level, the audio thread will drop frames. However, the cb_level of capture streams are 256 from ARC++ and 480 from Chrome. Both of them * 2 are less than 1024, it causes the overrun ops will be triggered every time. To fix the problem, we can add the overrun op threshold. The op only works when the hw_level is larger than that threshold. That time must to be longer than 2048 frames with rate 48000 (grunt only supports 48000 rate). Therefore, we think 50ms is a reasonable threshold. For users, it means that the delay will be reduced only if it is larger than 50ms. The value is too small to affect the user experience. Notice that we can not fix the problem by changing a period size on grunt because it will change a buffer size, too. (Buffer size = 2 * period size on grunt. See #22 on b/112860209) BUG=b:138076270, chromium:918462 TEST=The capture frames is not dropped on grunt and the delay keeps in 50ms on panther. xkeyboard-config: drop brokenbar from Swiss (German) layout Historically, the Swiss (German) layout has had two vertical bar characters: * Senkrechter Strich (U+007C, vertical line) * Unterbrochener Strich (U+00A6, broken bar) The broken bar is a relic from old school mechanical typesetting to have a character that looked different from uppercase-I and lowercase-l. Nowadays, the character does not have use for a typical user and only serves as a point of confusion when shells treat it differently from the regular vertical bar. For what it's worth, upstream xkeyboard-config and Mac OS X do not have this character in their layout. Windows appears to still have the character (at least in Windows 7). In the interest of reducing the number of Chrome OS specific patches to xkeyboard-config and reducing user confusion, we should drop this patch. Thanks to ricop@ on eng-misc for helping explain the historical context of this character.
